question: Use a ridge plot to compare the distribution of tumor mutational burden (TMB) across 10 cancer types.

files.eval_guideline: Ridge plot must show TMB density distributions for all 10 cancer types as stacked overlapping curves; axis labels, color scheme, and cancer type ordering may differ.
files.match_reasoning: The files have the identical basename and PNG image format. Their shared task identifier and ridge-plot naming clearly indicate that both represent the requested TMB distribution visualization.
files.strategy_reasoning: The guideline requires semantic visual content: density distributions for all 10 cancer types shown as stacked overlapping curves, while permitting stylistic and ordering differences. A semantic image comparison is therefore appropriate.

comparison_details.explanation: Both images present ridge plots of TMB density distributions for the same 10 cancer types in the same descending order: Melanoma, Lung Adenocarcinoma, Bladder, Colorectal, Head & Neck, Stomach, Breast, Pancreatic, Ovarian, and Prostate. The principal distribution patterns agree: melanoma has the highest and broadest TMB distribution with a long right tail, lung adenocarcinoma and bladder are intermediate-high, colorectal and head-and-neck are centered slightly lower, and breast, pancreatic, ovarian, and prostate concentrate at low TMB values. Both use a comparable horizontal TMB range and correctly label the TMB axis. The candidate adds sample sizes and numerical medians, marks each median with a dashed line, and uses a different color palette and label placement; these are informative stylistic additions rather than scientific discrepancies. Minor differences in curve smoothness, apparent peak heights, and the upper x-axis limit do not materially alter the distributions or overall scientific message.
